pcb_considerations.assertion: For the VBAT supply, keep the input voltage from falling below 3.0 V during a 2 A transmit burst; make VBAT PCB traces at least 60 mil wide and place the power IC and bypass capacitor close to the module.
Keep antenna trace from pin output to connector as short as possible; do not route RF signal across the board; keep RF away from the SIM card and power ICs.

Keep the positive VBAT line short and wide; route source to VBAT through the Zener diode and then the large capacitor; make the shortest layout from pins 2/43/44/45 to the power-source GND. Do not route signals on the upper layer of the 12 central GND pads if possible.

Keep the SIM holder away from the antenna/RF cable, place it close to the module, and protect SIM_CLK, SIM_DATA, SIM_RST and SIM_VDD with ESD components; keep those signals away from power and high-frequency signals.
Keep audio traces away from the antenna and power and avoid routing audio in parallel with VBAT; trace UART and USB signal lines bundled.
For the USB debug interface, the TVS on the USB data line should be less than 5 pF and USB data must be routed differentially; reserve the USB interface or a test point for debugging.

For the SIM interface, use short traces, keep them away from RF/VBAT/high-speed signals, connect SIM-holder GND directly to main ground, use a 100 nF SIM_VDD capacitor close to the holder, TVS parasitic capacitance no more than 50 pF, and 51 ohm resistors on SIM_RST/SIM_CLK/SIM_DATA for improved ESD protection.

antenna_requirements.assertion: There are three antenna ports: GSM_ANT, BT_ANT, and FM_ANTP/FM_ANTN; each RF interface has 50 ohm impedance.
The antenna input impedance should be 50 ohm and VSWR should be less than 2; place GSM and BT antennas as far apart as possible and keep isolation of the three antennas greater than 30 dB.
The GSM antenna connection must be DC-decoupled because the antenna connector is DC-coupled to ground through an inductor for ESD protection.
GSM matching components R101/C101/C102 are defined by antenna design; normally R101 is 0 ohm and C101/C102 are not mounted. Keep the conducted-test RF connector close to GSM_ANT.

Bluetooth matching components R201/C201/C202 are defined by antenna design; normally R201 is 1.2 nH, C202 is 1.5 pF, and C201 is not mounted. Keep RF traces 50 ohm and away from high-frequency signals and strong disturbing sources.
FM_ANTP and FM_ANTN are differential FM antenna pads; the document presents both an FM matching circuit and an earphone-GND-as-FM-antenna alternative.

protection_circuits.assertion: A 5.1 V / 500 mW Zener diode at VBAT is strongly recommended for voltage-surge protection; place it and the capacitors as close as possible to the VBAT pins.
Table 6 names MMSZ5231BT1G, PZ3D4V2H, MMSZ4689-V, and CDZ55C5V1SM as recommended 500 mW Zener diodes.
All SIM-interface signals should be protected against ESD with a TVS diode array; the SIM application text recommends an ESD component such as ST ESDA6V1-5W6 or ON SEMI SMF05C.
D101 in the GSM antenna circuits is used for ESD protection; the text says TVS can be used and recommends Marata LXES03AAA1-154 (0201) or LXES15AAA1-153 (0402).
The USB data-line TVS should be less than 5 pF.

ambiguities.description: The physical-page-15 text extraction splits and reorders multiple labels (for example STATUS and RF_SYNC). The complete pinout is therefore transcribed from the tabular pin description on physical pages 16–18, rather than inferred from the diagram geometry.

The physical-page-18 figure is present but its numerical dimension callouts are not legible in the text extraction. The dimensions reported above come from the explicit physical-characteristics text/table on page 13, not from the figure.

On physical page 55, the extracted layout places the mA unit on shared/separate lines for some voice and data-mode rows. Values are preserved as their table-associated band sequences; no additional mode values are inferred.

The figure index calls Figure 31 “Speaker with amplifier reference circuit,” while the physical-page-35 extraction shows MIC1P/2P, MIC1N/2N, an electret microphone, and ESD labels. That figure is not relied on for a speaker-circuit assertion beyond its documented title/indexing.

On physical page 61, sentences around “relative [humidity]” and the storage-humidity wording are visibly truncated in the text extraction. Only the explicit table values and untruncated requirements are used.
The pin-description table labels CTS (pin 34) “Request to send” and RTS (pin 33) “Clear to send.” These labels are retained exactly as supplied and have not been normalized to conventional naming.
